metrics.insight: The productivity fall is a tail, not a slide. The 65 heaviest books of a year ago fell -40.9%, $23.2M → $13.7M, while the other 584 paired AEs came in flat in aggregate — $63.2M → $63.0M, -0.2%. 268 of 649 paired AEs sold more than they did a year ago and 381 sold less, on a median index of 91. form.note: Geometry contract for the renderer. Each fan line is one quota-carrying AE present on BOTH the FY26 Q2 and FY27 Q2 rosters, drawn from a common origin on the left to its indexed position on the right. The origin is an index rather than a dollar value, so no AE's baseline is implied to be any other's — and the population is restricted to the paired roster, so no line is a comparison against an AE who was not there.
form.indexOf: round(currentK / priorK * 100) — 100 is flat, 0 is an AE who booked nothing this quarter, 295 is the largest rise in the population
form.lineWeightBy: priorK — the finding is only visible if the AEs who carried the biggest books last year read heavier than the rest
form.marginalDensity: Kernel or binned density of the index values along the right axis, computed from rows rather than authored, so it cannot disagree with the lines it sits beside
form.bandwidthNote: Silverman's rule on this population: 0.9 × min(sd 64, IQR/1.34 64.9) × n^(-1/5) = 15.77, rounded to 16. The account population it replaced gave 13.9, which would have been the wrong smooth here.

overflow.renderAs: An explicit chevron above the top of the axis carrying the count, and the overflowing lines terminate on the axis top rather than at their own value. Silently clamping them to the top tick — which is what the [0, 200] range did before it was widened — draws them as though they landed there.
overflow.note: The account population this range was set for never overflowed: its largest expansion was 194 against a ceiling of 200. At AE grain 22 of 649 AEs are past 250, the largest at 295, so the clamp would have fired silently on every one of them.

flatBand.note: 21 of 649 paired AEs land within 2 index points of the reference. That is 3.2% of the population, which is small enough to draw: the movers-only treatment the account fan's exclusion stub would have supported is not needed here, because year-over-year ACV per AE is not a measure that holds still. Stated so the decision is visible rather than assumed.

generator.note: This population is generated, not hand-typed. The rule is stated here so anyone can reproduce the rows exactly and confirm the distribution is a consequence of a stated rule rather than authored noise shaped to look convincing. Written by scripts/author-ae-fan.mjs.
generator.prng: 32-bit LCG. s(k+1) = (1103515245 * s(k) + 12345) mod 2^31, u(k) = s(k) / 2^31. Draws are consumed in emission order within each stream.
generator.emissionOrder: Paired AEs by prior-year rank 1-649, then 96 joiners, then 255 leavers. Row ids AE-001 to AE-649, AE-J001 to AE-J96, AE-L001 to AE-L255 follow that order, so an id is determined by the rule rather than assigned.
steps: 1. Paired split: the two rosters are 904 and 745. 96 joiners and 255 leavers are authored, which fixes the paired population at 745 - 96 = 904 - 255 = 649. The two identities have to agree or the script refuses to write.

2. Prior-year book: weight w(r) = r^-0.45 by rank r, apportioned across 86,350 by the largest-remainder method. 0.45 rather than the account population's 0.8, because every AE carries a quota — the top of an AE distribution is bounded by what one person can sell, which is not true of an account.

3. One LCG draw u per AE. Expansion propensity RISES with rank: p(r) = 0.33 + (0.72 - 0.33) * (r - 1) / (n - 1). The AEs who carried the biggest books are the least likely to have grown — that is the mechanism the panel is describing, so it is in the rule rather than added afterwards.

4. Movement multiplier m: if u < p then m = 1 + undefined * (u / p)^1.5, else m = 1 - undefined * ((u - p) / (1 - p))^0.7. maxDown = 1.0, so an AE can book nothing and no less. Any m <= 0.05 snaps to 0.
5. This year's book: largest-remainder apportionment of 76,720 across priorK * m, so currentK sums to the paired total exactly.
6. Joiners: priorK = 0, currentK apportioned across w(r) = r^-0.45 against 5,280. Leavers: currentK = 0, priorK apportioned the same way against 27,540.

7. segment is a stated threshold on the AE's basis value in $K (priorK, or currentK for a joiner): >= 260 enterprise, >= 110 commercial, else growth — territory segment, not a segment of the AE. region is one weighted LCG draw per AE — AMER 0.46, EMEA 0.28, APAC 0.18, LATAM 0.08.

rules.title: Zero baseline
rules.body: Every value axis starts at zero. A padded baseline makes each decline look steeper, and at this size nobody would notice it had been truncated.

rules.title: Additivity and period to date
rules.body: Direction of good is a decision this board makes and states — no measure in this layer declares one, so attrition reading as lower-is-better is the tab's doing rather than the definition's. What the layer does guarantee is additivity, that a measure sums correctly across grains, and a period-to-date flag on the measures that accumulate. Without that flag a half year is compared against a full one, which is the comparison this tab exists to refuse.
